newsitem.title: UK: First Leisure surges on Bass bid report.
newsitem.headline: First Leisure surges on Bass bid report.

text.p: Shares in First Leisure Corp Plc put on 4.5 percent, or 14p, to 325p in a sharply weaker overall market after a report said Bass Plc may be mulling a 650 million stg bid for the bingo and disco operator.
"It's logical that it would be pretty positive for the shares," said a market-maker.
Bass fell 12-1/2p to 815p amid a general sell-off.

The Sunday Times newspaper said First Leisure was a vulnerable target, particularly because its share price had languished since former Channel Four boss Michael Grade took over as executive chairman in June. The shares fell sharply after disappointing results and a profit-warning issued on June 24.
On July 11 the Daily Mail newspaper revived speculation which hit the market in mid-June that Rank Group Plc might bid for First Leisure. Rank dipped 8-1/2p to 327p.
Market rumours have also linked Bass's name to a possible bid for Ladbroke Group Plc after the British government blocked Bass's buy of the Carlsberg-Tetley brewing group.
